svg.text: XPU2: an asynchronous CPU + GPU path tracer
Core architecture, 25 October 2026. One work grid; each device takes its own work; any sample can be rendered by either device, from its identity.
Host application · showcase: MoonRay for Modo (xpu2_session.cc)
sends the scene and each edit; takes pictures, outputs and progress back; can stop, drain or hold a frame
XPU2 talks to its host through one session program; nothing else in the core knows the host
Reference renderer · MoonRay XPU
the image XPU2 converges to
renders, whole, any scene XPU2 refuses
scene and edits
refused: the whole scene
Scene indexer (entity_classes.h, routing_index.h)
every scene object and attribute, kept incrementally
classifier: each object is Both, CPU only or Fallback,
with the GPU feature families it needs
router: one decision per object, redone only for what
an edit touched
scene mode: both devices · CPU only · fallback
Plan (cpu_scene.h)
flat records both devices read: geometry, materials and
their map programs, lights and light tree, volumes,
textures as mip pyramids, the camera, the outputs
unchanged parts reused across edits by signature;
a camera-only edit changes only the camera
built from the reference renderer's scene (today MoonRay's RDL)
the plan
Scheduler: the cellular work grid (async_grid.h, device_suit.h, async_adaptive.h)
Work grid
8 px tiles in 64 px cells
a chunk: one tile and a range of
sample indices
each chunk claimed once, by one
atomic in host memory
ranges of 1, 1, 2, then 4 samples:
the whole picture first
Ownership
cells start on the suited device:
a first-hit probe, comparative
advantage; else a checkerboard
flips follow the measured shares
(at most 8 a frame, cooldown, freeze)
important parts first: busy cells
stay with their owner, a range ahead
Cellular workers
CPU threads and 32 GPU workers
(shares of each GPU launch)
finish the cell · own reserved · open ·
by passage; neighbours first
rights of passage: enter the other
device's cells only where that can't
hold the frame up
Sampling generations
every pass is a generation: tiles
above their target error sample again
uniform: samples go where the error
is, in uniform sampling's time
adaptive: until the target error
both lanes' errors pooled by count
Memory tiers (textures)
host RAM: every level of every texture, the system of
record; the CPU lane reads it directly and never misses
VRAM: levels 1 and up for the session, plus a cache of
fine (level 0) tiles, least recently used, sized from
the card's free memory
GPU broker (async_render.h)
one pinned host thread claims chunks for the GPU
two launches always queued, each about 10 ms of work
at the GPU's measured rate
polls events: the host never waits for the GPU
near the end, splits the rest so both finish together
workers claim
their own chunks
claims for the GPU
mailbox ring of chunks
CPU lane (async_cpu.h)
persistent, pinned workers; Embree traversal
renders every feature XPU2 has
takes the samples the GPU defers and renders each
whole from its identity: no path state crosses devices
renders provisional samples again in full
reads every texture level from host RAM; its own film
light filters, shadow linking, lobe light sets and
emissive volumes keep a whole scene on the CPU lane today
GPU lane (async_gpu.h, OptiX)
launches as wide as the card holds; each thread claims one
sample at a time, neighbours in neighbouring pixels
acceleration structures kept while a mesh is unchanged
stand-ins for what only the CPU renders: a sample
that meets one is deferred to the CPU lane
a fine texture tile not resident: finished a level up,
provisional, rendered again in full later
its own film, in double precision; the program in
modules, compiled in parallel
deferred samples
(pixel, index, pass)
provisional samples
(pixel, index, tile, value)
or back to the GPU once
their tile has landed
every sample
every sample
Shared integrator (async_integrator.h)
one source compiled for both devices (X2_HD), run through each lane's own backend for traversal and textures
a sample's random numbers come from its identity (pixel, sample index, seed), so any device makes the same sample
implements the reference renderer's estimator and shading: today MoonRay's path tracer and shader library, ported
bounce-ray reuse: a BSDF sample that reaches a light and goes on as a bounce needs no shadow ray of its own
Films and the frame's end
one film per lane, merged when the frame ends; every pixel's sample count audited: no sample lost or counted twice
provisional samples are shown in the pictures but kept out of the film; none are left when the frame ends
outputs as the reference renderer writes them: beauty, AOVs, light path expressions, Cryptomatte, display filters
an image is XPU2's or the reference renderer's, whole: never a mix of the two
pictures, outputs and progress to the host
each pass's errors steer the next generation
